chunks: BJT vs MOSFET (MOSFET perspective). The question: What is the difference between a BJT and MOSFET?
A BJT and a MOSFET both act as electronic switches or amplifiers, but you control them differently. A BJT needs a steady base current to stay on.
A MOSFET needs only a voltage on its insulated gate. That one difference explains most of why MOSFETs dominate switching.
Think of two ways to keep a door open. A BJT is like holding it with your hand: as long as you keep pushing, it stays open.
A MOSFET is like setting a latch: you push once and it stays. The comparison fails on one point. A MOSFET gate still needs a short burst of current each time it switches.
The BJT's g m grows linearly with current; a MOSFET's grows only as √I, and you need a much wider device (bigger k n, i. e. , more W/L) just to approach the BJT.
This is why bipolar input stages are still used in low-noise and high-gain analog.
Base current: the steady current a BJT needs. About collector current divided by beta, the BJT's current gain (often about 100).
Gate capacitance: why the MOSFET gate takes current only during switching. V CE(sat) and R DS(on) : a BJT's fixed drop when on, versus a MOSFET's resistance when on.
Transconductance: how much output current changes per volt of input. BJTs have more per milliamp. Saturation: in a BJT it means fully on.
In a MOSFET it means constant-current mode.
Say you want to carry 1 amps. A BJT with a beta of 100 needs about 10 milliamps of base current the whole time it is on.
A MOSFET needs essentially zero current once the gate has charged. Neither is free, but the MOSFET's DC drive cost is far lower. That is the whole idea.
"A BJT is current-controlled through a forward-biased junction: it needs continuous base current, roughly I C over beta , and when on it has a fixed-ish V CE(sat) .
A MOSFET is voltage-controlled through an insulated gate: no DC gate current, and when on it's a resistor, R DS(on) . MOSFETs switch faster and parallel easily.
BJTs have more transconductance per milliamp and lower noise, so they still win in some analog.
And watch the names: BJT saturation is fully on, MOSFET saturation is the amplifier region."
